candidates.summary: chromeShot's only health check is a non-zero file size, so a page that never rendered and a URL the server 404s both pass as successful screenshots
candidates.failure_scenario: chromeShot returns nil whenever Chrome exits 0 and the PNG is larger than zero bytes. Measured at this head with Google Chrome 152.0.7977.75: a page whose body paints after the 4 s --virtual-time-budget (shots.go:180) screenshots byte-identical to a page that never paints at all (slow=2bff94039a8c blank=2bff94039a8c, rendered=dd6a7608aad4), and a URL the local file server answers 404 for screenshots the '404 page not found' body in 6743 bytes. Both come back with err == nil, so ScreenshotPairs sets pair.After (line 83) or pair.Before (line 92) and comment.go's pairGrid publishes the image under 'after - this PR'. A slow before-half plus a fast after-half prints a blank 'before' beside a rendered 'after', which reads to the reviewer as content this PR added.

candidates.summary: a failed chromeShot leaves the partial or zero-byte PNG in _shots/, which ships inside the published snapshot
candidates.failure_scenario: chromeShot returns an error at shots.go:185 or 188 without removing out; the 188 branch is reached precisely because the file exists with zero bytes. ScreenshotPairs then continues without setting pair.After, so nothing in preview.json references it, but _shots/ sits under outDir and the whole directory is uploaded as the snapshot artifact and served from the preview site. Every failed render adds a dead 0-byte <realm>-after.png to the published tree.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:184-190: neither error return calls os.Remove(out), and the size==0 branch proves the file was created
candidates.evidence: shots.go:187 'if fi, err := os.Stat(out); err != nil || fi.Size() == 0 { return fmt.Errorf("chrome wrote no image") }' - the stat succeeded, so the file is there and stays

candidates.summary: the realm's snapshot link is spelled here as path.Dir(afterFile)+"/" and again in comment.go as TrimPrefix(path.Dir(urlToFile(u)),"/"), two spellings of one mapping in one binary
candidates.failure_scenario: ShotPair.URL is built from the crawled file path, while comment.go:175 and comment.go:149's tabs() rebuild the same URL-to-snapshot-path mapping from the URL. The two already disagree in shape: this one appends a slash and keeps a leading path component, the other trims a leading slash. A change to urlToFile's layout (a new _a/_t segment, a different listing suffix) has to be mirrored in both, and a miss shows up as a 404 behind a published image rather than as a build failure.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'path.Dir' misc/gnopreview/shots.go misc/gnopreview/comment.go: shots.go:77 against comment.go:175-176, same mapping, two spellings
